evals.prompt: Draft an ADR for choosing an asynchronous report queue. The repository stores ADRs under docs/decisions with numbered Markdown files and an index. The current report handler is synchronous, and the agreed proposal accepts jobs then polls for completion. Retention is undecided. Do not implement anything.
evals.expected_output: Creates one proposed record in the existing convention with current facts, choice, trade-offs, and an explicit retention gap.
assertions: Finds local ADR numbering and index before writing
Distinguishes current synchronous code from proposed queue behavior
Keeps retention unresolved
Does not implement the queue or mark the ADR accepted

evals.prompt: Supersede accepted ADR-004 with a new decision. The approval record confirms ADR-009 is accepted. Keep ADR-004's decision text, update the index, and link both records.
evals.expected_output: Preserves historical decision text and records a traceable, bidirectional supersession with consistent index status.
assertions: Reads the approval evidence and current statuses
Does not rewrite ADR-004's accepted decision
Links ADR-004 and ADR-009 both ways
Checks the index and links after editing

evals.prompt: Review this proposed ADR. It says a cache is already deployed, but the code only has a proposal branch. It marks itself accepted with no approval record. Do not edit the file.
evals.expected_output: Reports the unsupported deployed and accepted claims in a read-only review.
assertions: Keeps Review read-only
Checks implementation versus proposal evidence
Names the missing acceptance evidence
Gives concrete corrections

evals.prompt: Write a broad RFC comparing three storage services, rollout plans, and acceptance criteria. We have not chosen an architecture yet.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Proposal job in write-adr and asks super-architecture for a recommendation only when needed; it does not fabricate an accepted ADR.
assertions: Selects the Proposal job
Keeps the architecture choice open
Does not fabricate an accepted decision

evals.prompt: Write an RFC proposing asynchronous report generation. Code currently handles reports synchronously. The proposal returns a job identifier and polling URL, targeting request acceptance within one second. Compare continued synchronous processing. Retention duration is unresolved and belongs to the data owner. Write the design document only, not code or tickets.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Proposal job to separate current facts from proposed behavior, compare a realistic alternative, and make acceptance reviewable.
assertions: Labels job and polling behavior proposed
Records measurable acceptance without claiming it passed
Explains the choice, alternative, trade-offs, and rollout
Keeps retention as an open decision
Does not implement code or create tickets

evals.prompt: Revise an accepted cache ADR with a new proposal. The implementation caches per tenant, but a stale plan describes one global cache. Git history explains that tenant isolation followed a previous incident. We have no performance measurements for the proposed eviction policy. Preserve the old decision record and make the new choice reviewable.
evals.expected_output: Uses the ADR job, preserves the accepted record, reconciles current code and history against the stale plan, and labels the eviction policy as proposed.
assertions: Reports the plan versus implementation disagreement
Uses relevant Git history without reviving the stale plan
Preserves accepted history with a new or superseding proposal
Does not invent measured performance or acceptance

evals.prompt: The report-generation RFC is accepted. Produce implementation tickets and ordered coding tasks with acceptance tests. Do not rewrite the design document.
evals.expected_output: Routes execution planning to write-plan and ticket work to create-tickets rather than authoring another proposal.
assertions: Routes implementation planning to its owner
Does not create another RFC or change the accepted decision
Does not implement code while producing the plan

evals.prompt: Write an RFC with an infographic comparing the current synchronous report flow with a proposed queued design. A current-flow diagram is already verified. Proposed latency improvement is unmeasured. Use a visual comparison rather than implementing the proposal.
evals.expected_output: Uses infographic for the requested comparison, reuses the verified diagram as needed, and preserves the current/proposed distinction.
assertions: Selects infographic as the visual owner
Keeps current behavior, proposed architecture, and unmeasured performance distinct
Avoids a diagram/infographic callback loop
Produces no unrequested code or duplicate asset
